schema.name: Ship HP
schema.description: Your ship's maximum HP (hull), together with formation, booster and lab bonuses. Also changes while the game is running.

schema.name: Ship shield
schema.description: Your ship's maximum shield (shield generators on the ship and drones, with bonuses). Also changes while the game is running.

schema.name: Ship speed
schema.description: Your ship's flight speed (with speed generators and bonuses). Effects like slowdowns and Fortify still apply.

schema.name: Shield regeneration
schema.description: How fast the shield refills by itself out of combat (game value 4% per second). 0: the shield never refills by itself.

schema.name: Repair bot speed
schema.description: How fast the repair bot (REP) repairs the hull.

schema.name: Your hit chance
schema.description: Hit chance of your lasers, rockets and P.E.T. (game value 80%, at most 100%). x1.25: every shot hits.

schema.name: Rocket cooldown
schema.description: Cooldown and reload time of rockets and the rocket launcher. Lower value: more frequent shots.

schema.name: Invulnerable ship
schema.description: Alien shots are shown, but your ship loses no hit points or shield.

schema.name: Infinite ammo
schema.description: Laser ammo, rockets, launcher ammo and mines are not used up (you need at least one).

schema.name: Infinite tech
schema.description: Tech items (Energy Leech, Battle Repair Bot, Speed Burst …) are not used up when activated (you need at least one). Cooldowns still apply.

schema.name: Your own mines hurt you
schema.description: The blast of a mine you placed also damages your ship (as in the game). When off, only aliens are hit.

schema.name: HP on on-the-spot repair
schema.description: HP you get when you repair on the spot after your ship is destroyed (game value 10%; the shield starts empty).

schema.name: Protection after on-the-spot repair
schema.description: How long you take no damage after repairing on the spot (game value 10 s). Ends when you fire.

schema.name: Damage from aliens
schema.description: Damage aliens (NPCs) deal to your ship, your P.E.T. and friendly ships. 0: you take no damage at all.

schema.name: On maps
schema.description: Aliens and bosses roaming the maps.

schema.name: In gate and mode waves
schema.description: Aliens in the waves of Galaxy Gates, event gates and modes (Astral, EBL, Voyagers, Trinity, Mimesis …).

schema.name: Damage you deal
schema.description: Damage you deal to aliens, players and bots with lasers, rockets, launchers, mines, Smart Bomb, cannons, the P.E.T. and abilities.

schema.name: Vs aliens (PvE)
schema.description: Damage you deal to aliens (NPCs).

schema.name: Vs players (PvP)
schema.description: Damage you deal to other players with lasers and rockets.

schema.name: Vs bots
schema.description: Damage you deal to bots.

schema.name: Alien hit points and shields
schema.description: Alien hit points and shields. A lower value kills aliens faster.

schema.name: On maps
schema.description: Aliens and bosses roaming the maps.

schema.name: In gate and mode waves
schema.description: Aliens in the waves of Galaxy Gates, event gates and modes (Astral, EBL, Voyagers, Trinity, Mimesis …).

schema.name: Alien hit chance
schema.description: Chance that aliens hit your ship and P.E.T. (game value 60%, at most 100%). 0: they never hit.

schema.name: Alien speed
schema.description: Flight speed of aliens (stationary ones stay put).

schema.name: Alien aggression
option_description: As in the game: aggressive types attack when they see you, the others fight back when shot.
Every alien chases and attacks you once it notices you.
No alien attacks on its own; an alien you shoot still fights back.
schema.description: Whether aliens chase you on their own (including those in gate and mode waves).

schema.name: Alien detection range
schema.description: Distance at which aggressive aliens notice you and start chasing (game value 1,000 units).

schema.name: Alien firing range
schema.description: Distance from which aliens can fire lasers, rockets and bombs at you (game value 450 for most, 550 for Kristallons, 1,000 for stationary ones; world boss attacks included).

schema.name: Slowing alien shots
schema.description: Shots from aliens such as Barb, The Stinger, Saboteur and Mindfire Behemoth slow your ship down. When off, they only deal damage.

schema.name: Attacking your own company
schema.description: You can attack players and bots from your own company (as in the game): forbidden on your company's X-1 and X-2 maps, destroying them brings a penalty. When off, you cannot attack your own company (except clans at war).

schema.name: Radiation damage
schema.description: Hull damage from radiation outside the map border. 0: radiation does no harm.

schema.name: Clan Battle Station HP
schema.description: Health and shield of every Clan Battle Station module (yours, bot clans' and rival clans'). When changed, the modules' current health scales proportionally; in-game bars refresh when you re-enter the map or a module is hit.

schema.name: Clan Battle Station damage
schema.description: Damage dealt by the weapon modules of every Clan Battle Station (to aliens, and by a rival station to you).

schema.name: Battle station shields
schema.description: Other clans' Clan Battle Stations are protected by their deflector shield while it is up. When off, their deflectors don't stop your attacks: a station another clan has just built can be destroyed at once and the asteroid taken. Your own station's deflector still protects it.

schema.description: Credits earned from aliens, boxes, missions, gates and events (sales and refunds excluded).

schema.description: Amount of ammo, resources, keys and tech items given by quests, Galaxy Gates, event gates, modes (Astral, EBL, Mimesis, Galaxy Trek …), Urgent Missions and Dispatch. Single items such as ships, lasers and designs stay at one; money and EP use their own multipliers.

schema.name: Item drop chance
schema.description: Chance that aliens drop boosters, equipment, resources and event boxes; Galaxy Gate lucky rewards (at most 100%).

schema.name: Booster
schema.description: Booster drops from Boss and Uber aliens.

schema.name: Extra alien rewards
schema.description: Palladium, event currency and resources you get for destroying an alien.

schema.name: Event drops
schema.description: Boxes from event and event gate aliens, Chromin boxes, Hitac lottery letters.

schema.name: Gates
schema.description: Lucky rewards of Galaxy Gates and event gates (designs, LF-4 …).

schema.name: Modes
schema.description: Astral's salvage core and keys, EBL's extra reward.

schema.name: Reduced X-1 cargo and rewards at high level
schema.description: On X-1 maps the aliens' cargo boxes shrink as your level rises (level 7: 50%, 10 and up: none), and on your own X-1 map kill rewards drop too (level 15 and up: none; as in the game). When off, full cargo and rewards at every level.

schema.name: Alien tagging
schema.description: The first to fire at an alien tags it: its reward, quest count and cargo box belong to them (or their group), even if someone else finishes it. The tag drops if its owner does not hit for 15 seconds. If off, the reward goes to whoever lands the last hit.

schema.name: Player takes the bot's tag
schema.description: If you shoot an alien that a bot has tagged, the tag passes to you: reward, quest count and cargo box become yours (bots in your group still share). Not for aliens fought together such as Cubikon, Mindfire Behemoth and world bosses: there the reward is split between players and bots by damage dealt, and the cargo box goes to the top damage dealer. Has no effect while alien tagging is off.

schema.name: Shared rewards on group aliens
schema.description: Cubikon, Ice Meteoroids, Hitac and world bosses: the reward is split between players and bots by damage dealt, and the cargo box goes to the top damage dealer. If off, they follow the usual tagging rule: whoever tags it gets everything (handy for levelling up a friend).

schema.name: Cargo box ownership
schema.description: An alien's cargo box belongs to its owner only; others see it in blue (if the game's Settings > Display option for other players' cargo boxes is on). Collecting the box of someone from your own company costs honor: 10 for the first that day, twice as much each time. If off, anyone can collect it with no penalty.

schema.name: Drone experience
schema.description: Points your drones earn when you kill aliens: how fast drones level up.

schema.name: P.E.T. experience
schema.description: Experience your P.E.T. earns (game value 5% of the EP you earn): how fast the P.E.T. levels up.

schema.name: Season Pass points
schema.description: Points earned from Season Pass missions: how fast you level up the season.

schema.name: Season Pass duration
schema.description: Length of a season. The season starts from day 1 on the save's first login; when it ends, unclaimed rewards are booked and the next season starts (about 3 months in the real game). A change also applies to the running season.

schema.name: Battle Pass duration
schema.description: Length of the Battle Pass. When an event with a pass opens, the save's pass starts from day 1 and runs together with the event for this long (even if its calendar period ends sooner); one pass at a time (about 2 weeks in the real game).

schema.name: Booster strength
schema.description: The bonus of boosters (damage, HP, shield, EP, honor …) and the cap of each type. x2: a 10% damage booster gives 20%.

schema.name: Level Based Rank Threshold
schema.description: The old rank system: your rank cannot go above the one your rank points reach on the threshold table, even when your place in the company is higher (the same applies to bots). When off, only the place among the company's pilots decides the rank, so the company's best pilot is Chief General even at a low level. Without bots the thresholds always apply.

schema.name: Bonus box abundance
schema.description: Number of bonus boxes on the maps (event boxes included).

schema.name: Bonus boxes
schema.description: Bonus boxes scattered across the maps.

schema.name: Booty chests
schema.description: Booty chests opened with a key.

schema.name: Event boxes
schema.description: Boxes that events bring to the maps.

schema.name: Box respawn time
schema.description: Time until a collected box is replaced. Lower value: sooner.

schema.name: Alien count
schema.description: Number of aliens on the maps (bosses included; gate and mode waves excluded).

schema.name: Map aliens
schema.description: The map's own aliens and bosses.

schema.name: Event aliens
schema.description: Aliens that events bring to the maps.

schema.name: Alien respawn time
schema.description: Time until a dead alien is replaced. Lower value: sooner.

schema.name: Ore abundance
schema.description: Number of collectable ores (Prometium, Endurium, Terbium …) on the maps.

schema.name: Ore respawn time
schema.description: Time until a collected ore is replaced. Lower value: faster.

schema.name: Quests at the same time
schema.description: How many quests you can run at the same time in the quest window (game value 5). When all slots are taken, no new quest can be accepted until one is completed or cancelled. Lowering it does not cancel running quests.

schema.name: Starter campaign
schema.description: The "Level N" starter quests are always shown in the quest window. When off, they show only for the first month and only if chosen when the save was created; a running quest can always be finished.

schema.name: Jump CPU occasionally misjumps
schema.description: With a small chance (2%) the jump CPU takes you to the Cubikon Graveyard (as in the game). When off, it always goes to the map you picked.

schema.name: Unique packages once
schema.description: Shop packages containing a ship, ship design, formation, P.E.T. or unique drone (Defcom-Raven, Stellar, Dusklight …) can be bought once, as in the game, and then leave the list. When off they can be bought again (content you already own is skipped).

schema.name: Hangar at portals
schema.description: You can also open the hangar and change equipment in the safe zone of portals (convenience; in the real game only at the station). When off, only at the station.

schema.name: Clan 48-hour rules
schema.description: After leaving a clan you cannot found or join another clan for 48 hours; the clan name/tag can only be changed every 48 hours. When off there is no waiting time.

schema.name: Gate part chance
schema.description: Chance of getting a gate part per energy in the Galaxy Gate generator (the game's value is 13%; the window's odds list changes too).

schema.name: Duplicate part becomes a missing one
schema.description: When you draw a gate part you already have, the chance that you get a missing part instead (game value 50%). 100%: no duplicate parts at all (until the gate is built).

schema.name: Gate energy amount
schema.description: Amount of free Galaxy Gate energy from bonus boxes (the Palladium trade at the 5-2 merchant and packages don't change).

schema.name: Gate prices
schema.description: Uridium price of energy in the Galaxy Gate generator and of extra lives at a gate. 0: free.

schema.name: Lives in gates
schema.description: Lives given when a Galaxy Gate or an event gate (Plutus, Quarantine …) is prepared (game value 5 for most gates).

schema.name: No lives lost in gates
schema.description: Being destroyed in a Galaxy Gate or an event gate costs no life: the gate is never lost.

schema.name: Aliens per wave
schema.description: Number of aliens in the waves of Galaxy Gates, event gates and modes (Astral, EBL, Voyagers, Trinity, Echoes). Guarding bosses stay single.

schema.name: Pause between waves
schema.description: Start, sub-wave and break times of gate and mode waves (Galaxy Gate: start 6 s, break 30 s). 0: no waiting.

schema.name: No gate and mode entry limits
schema.description: Event gates have no daily, yearly or one-time entry limits and no cooldowns; the free entries of Voyagers and Trinity never run out.

schema.name: Galaxy Gates with a bonus
schema.description: Number of gates in the gate window that have a timed bonus reward at the same time. Gates and rewards are picked at random at the start of each period; finish a gate before the period ends (Dispatch gate missions included) to get the bonus once. 0: no bonus.

schema.name: Gate bonus amount
schema.description: Size of the gate bonus (honor, uridium, ammo, log disks, keys); single items such as lasers and designs stay at one.

schema.name: Gate bonus period
schema.description: How often the bonus gates change (aligned to midnight; 24: every day). Changing it renews the selection right away.

schema.name: Shop prices
schema.description: Price of everything sold in the shop for credits and uridium.

schema.name: Sold for credits
schema.description: Everything priced in credits in the shop.

schema.name: Sold for uridium
schema.description: Everything priced in uridium in the shop.

schema.name: Event designs in the shop
schema.description: Ship, drone and P.E.T. designs from events (Galactic Strife's Arios and Neikos, Trial of Terrors' Dusklight, past seasons' designs …) are sold in the shop. If turned off they are hidden in the shop and can't be bought; they are earned only in their own events: Battle Pass key exchange, event and booty boxes, GG weekend gates, Season Pass. The shop's own designs are always sold.

schema.name: Service fees
schema.description: P.E.T. slots, repair and fuel; Skylab upgrades, instant finish, fast transport and robots; ship warp. 0: free.

schema.name: P.E.T.
schema.description: P.E.T. slots, repair and fuel.

schema.name: Skylab
schema.description: Upgrades, instant finish, fast transport and robots.

schema.name: Ship warp
schema.description: Bringing another of your ships to you without going to the hangar.

schema.name: Repair cost after death
schema.description: Uridium cost of repairing at the portal and on the spot.

schema.name: Ore sell price
schema.description: Credits and uridium you get for ores sold at the refinery (also shown in the window).

schema.name: Cargo capacity
schema.description: The ship's cargo space (together with Logistics, the cargo CPU and the P.E.T. protocol).

schema.name: Infinite cargo
schema.description: Cargo never fills up: every box and ore can always be collected without a "cargo full" warning.

schema.name: Infinite P.E.T. locator range
schema.description: The P.E.T.'s enemy and resource locator gears point to the nearest target on the map with no range limit.

schema.name: Free Assembly
schema.description: No materials are spent in the Assembly and Upgrade/Disassembly tabs; the client shows every material as sufficient. Production and wait times and daily use limits stay the same.

schema.name: Old upgrade system
schema.description: Item upgrades as in 2018, with uridium only: the Assembly's Upgrade tab no longer asks for ABR, Indoctrine Oil, Diametrion or other materials. The price is the old Item Upgrading's 100% success price (3,905 U. for level 2, +435 per level; 104,250 U. in total up to 16). Also changes while the game is running.

schema.name: Old upgrade prices
schema.description: Uridium price of upgrades in the old system (the Upgrade Hour discount still applies). 0: free.

schema.name: P.E.T. fuel use
schema.description: The P.E.T.'s fuel use per minute. 0: it uses no fuel.

schema.name: Skylab production
schema.description: Hourly output of Skylab collectors and refineries.

schema.name: Skylab storage capacity
schema.description: Capacity of the Skylab storage for each resource.

schema.name: Crafting and waiting times
schema.description: Assembly crafting, Skylab upgrades and transport, Dispatch missions, item upgrades. Lower value: faster (applies to newly started ones).

schema.name: Assembly crafting
schema.description: Crafting items in the Assembly.

schema.name: Skylab
schema.description: Module upgrades and transport.

schema.name: Dispatch
schema.description: Missions and gate runs.

schema.name: Item upgrades
schema.description: Level upgrades of lasers, generators, drones and modules.

schema.name: Ability and item cooldowns
schema.description: Cooldown of ship abilities, CPUs, mines, Smart Bomb, Insta-Shield, tech items and special rockets.

schema.name: Ship abilities
schema.description: Your ship's own abilities.

schema.name: Combat items and CPUs
schema.description: Mines, Smart Bomb, Insta-Shield, EMP, special rockets and CPUs.

schema.name: Tech items
schema.description: Energy Leech, Chain Impulse, Battle Repair Bot, Speed Burst …

schema.name: Particle cannons and drive
schema.description: Particle weapons and the Singularity Drive.

schema.name: Booster duration
schema.description: How long boosters stay active (applies to newly activated ones).

schema.name: No level restrictions
schema.description: Portals and the jump CPU have no level requirement: you can enter every map.

schema.name: Session events always open
schema.description: Events that open at set hours (Vortex of Greed, Treacherous Domain, Mimesis Mutiny) stay open for the whole event: the portal is always open, and a session, battle or run starts when you enter. Event aliens (Curcubitor, Agatus, Lanatum, Chaos Protegit) also spawn outside the game's hourly windows.

schema.name: Virtual rivals
option_description: No rivals: only you place bids.
They place small bids now and then; they never outbid you, so any lot you bid on is yours.
More frequent and slightly higher bids; they still never outbid you.
When you outbid them they answer after a while. Go past their budget and the lot is yours; if you lose, your credits come back.
They answer very often, quickly and with big budgets. Bid well to keep the lot.
schema.description: Virtual bidders who compete with you at the auction. Timid and Moderate: they bid a little but never outbid you, so any lot you bid on is yours. Competitive and Aggressive: they answer when you outbid them; unless you go past their budget you may lose the lot (your credits come back). Off while a bot pack is running in the world: the bots bid instead.

schema.name: Dark maps (flashlight)
schema.description: On the Trial of Terrors gate maps the screen goes dark and only the direction your ship faces is lit (the client's flashlight effect). Turn it off for bright maps.

schema.name: Cinematic boss entrances
schema.description: When an event boss spawns and in a Galaxy Gate's last wave, the camera turns to the boss for a few seconds (controls are locked meanwhile), then returns to your ship.

schema.name: Beginner tips
schema.description: Tip windows when something happens for the first time (cargo full, out of ammo, another company's map) and as you level up, plus a description of the running event. Each shows once; tips you closed stay closed and can be reread in the tip archive.

schema.name: Kill streak announcements
schema.description: Destroy aliens in quick succession to get the "Triple Kill", "Unstoppable", "Godlike", "Like a Boss" announcement and sound (3, 6, 10, 15 kills; at most 10 s apart).

schema.name: Hide login pop-ups
schema.description: The daily bonus, tip and Season Pass windows that open at login are not sent (you can still open them from the menus).

schema.name: Admin mode
schema.description: You become an administrator in the game: an admin badge (yellow A) before your name, and you are left out of the rank system, the Hall of Fame rankings and the company ranking. Bots know you as an admin: they never attack you, follow your warnings in chat and react when they see you. On a friend server only for the host player.

schema.name: Admin ship
option_description: In admin mode you still show your own ship.
Admin ship (ship_admin): the same model as the game's UFO alien.
schema.description: In admin mode your ship looks like this; its stats (hit points, speed, equipment) are your own ship's.

schema.name: Spectator (invulnerable)
schema.description: In admin mode aliens and bots do not attack you and you take no damage; you can roam the maps freely and watch the bots.

schema.name: Admin in chat
schema.description: In admin mode your chat messages show as an admin's (in the game's admin colour).

schema.name: GM console
schema.description: The game's hidden admin window: in game press Ctrl, then Shift, then Z. Teleport to maps, spawn aliens and boxes, give items and packages, finish quests, set up gates, reset cooldowns, invulnerability. While on, an admin badge shows before your name (the client recognises the admin by rank 6000).

schema.name: Spawn aliens nearby
schema.description: Testing aid: one of each of the first four alien types spawns right next to your ship.

schema.name: Live test control channel
schema.description: Developer tool (control.py, 127.0.0.1:8099): message trace and request injection.

casual.name: Relaxed
casual.description: You take less damage; rewards and boxes are plentiful.

fast.name: Fast progress
fast.description: Five times the rewards; aliens are plentiful and respawn quickly.

hard.name: Hard
hard.description: Aliens hit harder and last longer, rewards are low, rivals are aggressive.

creative.name: Creative
creative.description: Your ship can't be destroyed, ammo never runs out, the shop and services are free, no waiting.
